title: God will provide (Genesis 22:1–19)
hookLine: the binding of Isaac, a hard story the Church reads as a figure of the Father's gift
carry: the two of them went on together

lines: A KNIFE, A BOY, AN ANGEL.
cards: Some stories you can't tidy up, and this is one of them. Jews call it the Akedah, the binding. Christians have painted it for centuries: a knife raised, a boy on the wood, an angel grabbing the old man's wrist.
People who love the Bible still argue about this chapter, and many find it disturbing. The Church doesn't ask anyone to find it easy.
It reads it on the holiest night of the year anyway, at the Easter Vigil, because it hears something in it worth the difficulty.

teach.h: THY ONLY BEGOTTEN, WHOM THOU LOVEST.
teach.b: First, the command. God tests Abraham. In the Douay-Rheims: "Take thy only begotten son Isaac, whom thou lovest."

Each phrase tightens: your son, your only one, the one you love, the laughing child of the promise. Go to a mountain in the land of Moria, and offer him there. The text gives no word of Abraham's feelings.
He rises early, saddles the donkey, splits the wood, in silence. Second, the walk. Three days.

Then Abraham puts the wood on Isaac's back, takes the fire and the knife in his own hands, and the two of them go on together. Isaac asks: father, here is the fire and the wood, but where is the victim?
Abraham answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "God will provide himself a victim for an holocaust, my son." And again: the two of them went on together. Third, the stopping.
At the top, Abraham builds the altar, binds Isaac, and raises the knife, and the angel of the Lord calls his name twice. Don't lay your hand on the boy.

teach.h: A RAM CAUGHT IN A THICKET.
teach.b: Abraham looks up and sees a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. He names the place: the Lord sees, or the Lord will provide. Fourth, how the Church reads it.
The Letter to the Hebrews says Abraham reckoned God could raise the dead. The Church Fathers saw Christ in Isaac carrying his own wood up a hill, and in the ram given in his place.

teach.h: A FIGURE OF THE FATHER'S GIFT.
teach.b: The Catechism reads it as a figure of the Father who does not spare his own Son.
Abraham's son was spared. The Church hears that the Father's Son was not.

how: Genesis 22 is one of the Old Testament readings at the Easter Vigil and is read on the Second Sunday of Lent in one year of the cycle; Jews read it at Rosh Hashanah and call it the Akedah.

practice: Don't try to solve today's story; just let one image stay: a father and son walking up a hill, side by side, the boy carrying the wood.
Let the questions come without chasing them away, since some stories are carried a long time before they open. If you pray, bring your questions to God as they are.

wordCard.voice: Akedah. The binding: the Hebrew name for Abraham's walk up the mountain with Isaac, which ends with a ram and a promise that God will provide. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: he will see, he will see to it. Abraham names the mountain the Lord will see, or provide.
